Further, there are three types of catatonia that have been classified, including akinetic, hyperkinetic, and malignant catatonia.[5]
One theory is that GABAergic (gamma-aminobutyric acid) neurotransmitters, which regulate both emotional and cognitive functions, become disrupted, leading to catatonic symptoms.[6]
